description:
Senegal has been reinstated as African football champions after a successful appeal at sport's highest court.
They beat Morocco one-nil in extra time in January's chaotic Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final in Rabat.
But were then stripped of the trophy in March because the team's players had walked off the pitch in protest during the match when Morocco were awarded a penalty. 
The Court of Arbiration for Sport (CAS) has now rejected the earlier ruling because the referee had allowed the match to resume.

Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque reports from Dakar, Senegal.

description:
Is freedom of movement a right or a privilege?

In this episode of @DohaDebates, host Dareen Abughaida is joined by David Engels, Gurminder Bhambra, Zahra Babar and David Oldroyd-Bolt to debate who gets to move freely - and why?

They examine the power of passports, the impact of empire and colonisation, citizenship, cultural change and the global inequalities shaping migration today. Should people be free to move across borders, or do states have the right to decide who enters and who can stay?

The views expressed in this episode are the guests’ own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance. Visit the @DohaDebates YouTube channel for the extended version.
